blocks.section: The block is no longer just attention plus an MLP

blocks.quote: The 2017 baseline is the original Transformer (\cite[Vaswani et al., 2017]{vaswani2017attention}); modern open-weight models keep its residual skeleton but replace several parts: RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, RoPE instead of additive position vectors, SwiGLU instead of GELU, grouped-query attention instead of full MHA, and usually a final normalization with a separate output head. The controls below change one forward pass of a four-token sentence.

blocks.quote: RoPE: position is a rotation, not an addition
blocks.section: RoPE: position is a rotation, not an addition

blocks.quote: Sinusoidal and learned schemes *add* a position vector to the token embedding. RoPE leaves the embedding alone and rotates the query and key vectors by an angle proportional to their position. The dot product of two rotated vectors depends on the **difference** of their angles, so the attention score becomes naturally relative (\cite[Su et al., 2021]{su2021rope}).

blocks.quote: The vectors are drawn in one two-dimensional frequency plane. RoPE rotates the query by m·ω and the key by n·ω . The dot product is cos((m−n)·ω) : only the relative offset survives. The second plot shows that relative score as the distance changes.

blocks.quote: What changed, and what stayed the same
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same
What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Normalization | LayerNorm (mean, gamma, beta) | RMSNorm (no mean, no beta) (\cite[Zhang & Sennrich, 2019]{zhang2019rmsnorm}) |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Position | added sinusoidal or learned vector | RoPE applied to Q and K |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Attention | MHA, one K/V head per query head | GQA (\cite[Ainslie et al., 2023]{ainslie2023gqa}); DeepSeek uses MLA instead |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Feed-forward | dense GELU, often 4× width | SwiGLU gate, no biases, narrower width (\cite[Shazeer, 2020]{shazeer2020glu}); large models may replace it with MoE |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Final norm | one final LayerNorm | final RMSNorm |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: | Output head | often tied to embeddings | usually separate |
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same

blocks.quote: The residual stream, causal mask, next-token cross-entropy and the idea “attention mixes, the FFN transforms” remain the same. This is why the modern block still reads as a Transformer, even though several named parts changed.
blocks.section: What changed, and what stayed the same
